text: A language model predicts the next token from earlier tokens. Training adjusts its weights to reduce prediction error.
The tokenizer turns text into token IDs. These IDs select rows from an embedding table. Token IDs are not probabilities.
The training split teaches the model. The development split helps choose a checkpoint. The test split measures the chosen checkpoint.
A causal mask hides future tokens. A prediction at the current position may use earlier positions but not the next answer.
A source document is evidence. A generated summary is a prediction. Keep every summary linked to the document that supports it.
A claim states a position. A premise gives a reason. A label depends on the task definition and cannot be assumed from a keyword.
A checkpoint saves model weights and optimizer state. To resume the same experiment, also restore random states and sampling state.
Cross entropy penalizes low probability on the observed next token. Perplexity is the exponential of mean negative log likelihood.
Training loss can fall while development loss rises. This may indicate memorization. Inspect the data and compare with a simple baseline.
Attention mixes values using weights from queries and keys. The weights show a computation, not automatic proof of a faithful explanation.
Gradient accumulation combines microbatches before an optimizer update. Divide the loss by the total number of valid target tokens.
An experiment changes one factor and keeps other factors fixed. Record the data, tokenizer, model, seed, configuration and measured result.
The small model runs on a local computer. Its purpose is to teach training mechanisms. It is not a reliable general assistant.
Byte pair encoding merges frequent adjacent pieces. Fit the merge rules on training documents only and save their exact order.
A duplicate document can leak across splits. Normalize text and check overlap before fitting. Exact checks do not detect every paraphrase.
Generated text may sound plausible and still be wrong. Evaluate claims against sources, study failures and report limits honestly.
The model learns a distribution over the next token. A small baseline helps us interpret whether the training run learned anything useful.
A summary needs evidence from its source. Correct formatting alone does not prove that the generated claims are supported.
Keep the test documents outside tokenizer fitting. Choose the best checkpoint using development loss instead of repeatedly selecting on test scores.
Restoring weights is not enough to restart training exactly. The optimizer, random generator and data sampler also have state.
The next token is a training target supplied by the text itself. It is not a human gold label for an argument classification task.
A model can memorize examples without transferring to new documents. Compare held out predictions and explain the limits of a tiny corpus.
The causal mask prevents future words from influencing earlier predictions. Padding is excluded from the loss so that shorter documents are not misweighted.
A reproducible result includes the tokenizer, configuration, data identity and model checkpoint. A dashboard should display real measurements instead of invented curves.
